newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian mining giant BHP reports profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Australian mining giant BHP reports profit fall.

text.p: Australian mining and energy giant Broken Hill Co Pty Ltd reported a 9.8 percent fall in first half profits on Friday.
Australia's largest company said it made a net profit A$790 million (US$628 million) for the six months to November 30, down from A$876 million for the same period a year ago.
BHP said profits in its steel division fell 39 percent to A$180 million, mainly due to lower export prices for Australia and New Zealand production.

Profits from its key copper division came in at A$217 million, down 32.2 percent on the same period last year. But petroleum sector profits surged by 69 percent to A$335 million, largely on the back of higher crude prices.
"The outlook for the group for the remainder of this financial year is, overall, moderately encouraging," BHP said in a results statement.

Market forecasts had varied widely on the BHP results. After rising briefly on news of the results, the BHP share price fell back to around A$17.20, 15 cents higher than Thursday's close, but off its earlier highs, as the market digested the figures.
